title: Evidence-Based Interventions programme: NHS low-value-procedure reduction and appropriateness rail
summary: Promotes Evidence-Based Interventions programme: NHS low-value-procedure reduction and appropriateness rail as a de-adoption/practice-lag infrastructure record. The record is not an incident or trial record; it describes a rail by which negative evidence can become reviewable, discussable, recommended against, or translated into practice constraints.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass source-backed extraction; child record and second-pass systematic-review extraction required for mature synthesis
limitations: Not medical advice and not a current clinical recommendation engine.
Uses exact indication/population/endpoints available in one-pass sources; child records needed for all subgroups and guideline dates.
Practice-lag claims require fuller utilization and reimbursement child records before maturity.
some recommendations are circumstance-specific rather than never-events
type_payload.query_value: A direct de-adoption rail for procedure-use practice lag, especially where evidence shows no benefit or harm.

handling_notes: Clinical reversals can involve real patients who made choices under uncertainty; avoid hindsight contempt.
Do not treat procedure de-adoption as a patient-specific treatment recommendation.
Preserve the difference between “no benefit in studied population” and “never useful.”

unknowns: This record has not yet extracted the full EBI intervention list, category history, or implementation metrics.

next_actions: Extract a versioned sample of EBI recommendations and map each to evidence source, implementation lever, and exception criteria.
